note: New uses of technology in war: first-seen or newly combined techniques observed in any theatre and any domain. Append-only. Each entry: id (YYYY-MM-DD-slug), date (when observed or first reported), theatre (board id), actor, t (headline), what (fact sentences with [n] citations), new (one or two sentences on what is new, in the reporters' and actors' terms, no prediction), domains (from the list below), src rows copied from the edition. The run checks ids and titles before appending so a technique is logged once; a later development of the same technique is a new entry that names the earlier id in prev.

items.t: A Shahed carried leaflets with a QR code that opened a phishing trap
items.what: A Shahed downed over Ukraine on 4 Nov carried printed leaflets with a QR code. Unmanned Systems Forces commander Robert Brovdi called it “a cyber-phishing trap activated when scanning a QR code”. [1]
items.new: A one-way attack drone used as a delivery vehicle for a cyber lure: the payload targets the phone of whoever picks up the wreckage, not the impact point.
src: Russia arming drones with propaganda, cyber threats, Ukraine's drone commander warns

items.t: Ambush drones perched on high-voltage power lines
items.what: Defense Express published video of Russian crews landing FPV ambush drones on high-voltage power lines, where they wait powered down for passing vehicles; the outlet describes it as a technique first used by Ukrainian crews and now copied. [1]
items.new: Power-line perches put the waiting drone above the clutter that ground-based detection searches, and the conductor height keeps it clear of infantry.
src: High-voltage power lines become new positions for Russian ambush drones

items.t: Russia links drones over Ukraine through its own low-orbit Rassvet satellites
items.what: Ukraine's military intelligence said on 6 Nov that Russia has launched 32 Rassvet satellites in March and July and uses them over Ukraine for military communications, including links to drones; an analyst counted at least two windows a day of more than an hour each. [96]
items.new: Reporters describe a two-way satellite data link from a Russian-owned low-orbit constellation, letting surveillance drones send live video and pilots re-route attack drones in flight instead of flying pre-set paths, outside the reach of ground-based jamming of line-of-sight links.
src: Russia using own version of Starlink for military comms over Ukraine, Kyiv says

items.actor: Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow (hackers); analysis reported by Bloomberg
items.t: Hacked Russian civil death records turned into a count of war dead
items.what: NOS, citing Bloomberg, reported on 9 Nov that hackers who breached Rosstat supplied more than 11 million death certificates, of which 392,700 from February 2022 to August 2026 name the war in the cause of death; Rosstat confirmed targeted cyberattacks but denied that confidential data were stolen. [28] Euronews gave the Cyber Partisans' figure as 393,881 to 27 Aug. [29]
items.new: Reporters describe a cyber intrusion into a state statistics registry followed by filtering of individual death certificates by age, residence and cause-of-death wording, which yields a casualty count independent of both governments' announcements.
src: Bijna 400.000 Russische doden in oorlog met Oekraïne, blijkt uit gehackte data
Rosstat hack: data obtained suggests over 390,000 Russian deaths in Ukraine war

items.actor: Russian airports, ports and power companies
items.t: Russian airports and ports buy remote-operated machine-gun turrets against drones
items.what: Militarnyi, citing Siberia.Realities, reported on 8 Nov that Surgut Airport tendered for “a turret system with two paired machine guns, a thermal imaging sight, a remote-operation monitor, and an external uninterruptible power supply”, the Port of Ust-Luga for three turrets, and Kolymaenergo bought one for fire teams at the Kolyma hydro plant. [97]
items.new: Civilian operators of airports, ports and power plants, not the armed forces, are buying remote-operated, thermal-sighted machine-gun mounts to shoot at drones over their own sites.
src: Russian Companies Begin Buying Machine Gun Turrets to Defend Against Drones (citing Siberia.Realities)

items.t: A smaller jet Geran-5 navigates with a camera-based correlation unit on a Chinese single-board computer
items.what: Ukrinform, citing Ukraine's defence intelligence (DIU), reported on 10 Nov that the Geran-5 K5-K, used against Ukrainian cities since early autumn, is 4 m long, cruises above 450 km/h at up to 6 km and carries a Susanin optical-electronic correlation unit that compares images from a dual-range camera with a stored reference image on a Coke Pi microcomputer; 52 of its 93 foreign electronic components are from US manufacturers. [31]
items.new: The DIU found the Susanin correlation unit, previously identified in the Geran-4, running a dual-range camera instead of optical sensors in a jet Geran it classes as a small cruise missile.
src: DIU examines new Russian Geran-5 K5-K drone: Nearly 100 foreign components, most of them American

items.actor: IRGC and Kataib Hezbollah (alleged by US prosecutors)
items.t: A jailed operative allegedly steered a UK air-base plot through coded calls to relatives
items.what: The US indictment unsealed on 10 Nov says Mohammad Baqer Saad Dawood al-Saadi, held in New York since May, passed coded messages in phone calls to his mother and sister in Iraq to coordinate co-defendants, while paid UK associates surveilled RAF Fairford and drove vans in fuel-delivery and pool-supply livery to its perimeter. [15, 14]
items.new: Prosecutors describe tasking relayed from a US detention facility through family phone calls to a cell that used commercial liveries and paid local helpers for surveillance and logistics against an air base.
src: US charges 3 men over alleged Iranian-backed plot at UK Fairford air base
Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says

items.actor: UK Ministry of Defence and Royal Navy
items.t: The Royal Navy buys North Atlantic undersea surveillance as a contracted service of drones, sensors and AI
items.what: The MoD announced on 10 Nov a £90 million framework with Ocean Infinity Solutions for Atlantic Net, a network of uncrewed systems and sensors in the North Atlantic that the Royal Navy directs as a single surveillance service cueing warships and Astute-class submarines against Russian submarines and threats to cables. [88]
items.new: A commercial operator brings maritime systems, underwater sensing, communications, remote operations and data services into one capability under naval direction, so persistent anti-submarine and cable surveillance is bought as a service rather than as platforms.
src: £90 million investment for new drones and sensors to protect undersea cables and hunt Russian submarines

items.t: Poland pays for Ukrainian counter-drone technology with life-expired MiG-29 fighters
items.what: Polish Deputy Defence Minister Tomczyk said on 10 Nov that Ukraine committed to transfer drone and counter-drone technologies in exchange for two MiG-29s past their service life, and that the two ministries signed an agreement on joint working groups on drone and counter-drone technology. [84, 83]
items.new: A NATO member acquires battlefield counter-drone technology from a country at war by bartering retired combat aircraft, government to government, alongside standing joint working groups rather than through an industry purchase.
src: MiGs for anti-drone systems. An agreement between Poland and Ukraine
Ukraine and Poland to establish joint working groups on drone and counter-drone technologies
